lines.cap: Listen closely. That’s the sound of a heart that has never needed a battery. Four beats every second, for as long as you wear it.
lines.say: Listen closely. That's the sound of a heart that has never needed a battery. Four beats every second, for as long as you wear it.

lines.cap: This is calibre 3235. It beats inside the Datejust, the Submariner Date and the Sea-Dweller. From the outside, it’s calm. But turn it over…
lines.say: This is calibre thirty-two thirty-five. It beats inside the Datejust, the Submariner Date, and the Sea-Dweller. From the outside, it's calm. But turn it over.

lines.cap: Open it up, and you’ll find something rather wonderful.
lines.say: Open it up, and you'll find something rather wonderful.

lines.cap: No battery. No circuitry. Just springs, wheels and jewels, every one with a job to do. So let’s take it apart, layer by layer.
lines.say: No battery. No circuitry. Just springs, wheels and jewels, every one with a job to do. So let's take it apart, layer by layer.

lines.cap: Lift the layers apart and the movement becomes a stack: the rotor on top, then bridges set with 31 synthetic rubies, tiny bearings that keep friction to a whisper. Then the balance, the escapement, the gear train, the barrel and the main plate.
lines.say: Lift the layers apart, and the movement becomes a stack. The rotor on top, then bridges set with thirty-one synthetic rubies, tiny bearings that keep friction to a whisper. Then the balance, the escapement, the gear train, the barrel, and the main plate.

lines.cap: It starts with the Perpetual rotor, patented by Rolex in 1931, and still one of the most elegant ideas in watchmaking. A half-moon of dense metal, it spins on a ball bearing every time your wrist moves, and reversing wheels turn every swing into winding force.
lines.say: It starts with the Perpetual rotor, patented by Rolex in nineteen thirty-one, and still one of the most elegant ideas in watchmaking. A half-moon of dense metal, it spins on a ball bearing every time your wrist moves, and reversing wheels turn every swing into winding force.

lines.cap: That winding flows into the mainspring, coiled inside the barrel. Rolex gave the barrel thinner walls, leaving room for a longer spring. Fully wound, it holds around 70 hours of power. Take it off on Friday evening, and come Monday morning, it’s still running.
lines.say: That winding flows into the mainspring, coiled inside the barrel. Rolex gave the barrel thinner walls, leaving room for a longer spring. Fully wound, it holds around seventy hours of power. Take it off on Friday evening, and come Monday morning, it's still running.

lines.cap: The spring lets that energy out slowly, through the gear train. The centre wheel turns once an hour for the minute hand. The fourth wheel turns once a minute for the seconds. Left alone, this train would simply race.
lines.say: The spring lets that energy out slowly, through the gear train. The centre wheel turns once an hour, for the minute hand. The fourth wheel turns once a minute, for the seconds. Left alone, this train would simply race.

lines.cap: So the escapement holds it back. The pallet fork catches the escape wheel, lets it slip half a tooth, and gives the balance a gentle push. Lock, release, impulse. That’s the tick you hear.
lines.say: So the escapement holds it back. The pallet fork catches the escape wheel, lets it slip half a tooth, and gives the balance a gentle push. Lock, release, impulse. That's the tick you hear.

lines.cap: Rolex’s Chronergy escapement is around 15 per cent more efficient than a conventional lever, and because it’s made of nickel-phosphorus, magnetism can’t throw it off.
lines.say: Rolex's Chronergy escapement is around fifteen per cent more efficient than a conventional lever. And because it's made of nickel-phosphorus, magnetism can't throw it off.

lines.cap: And here is the heart of the watch: the balance wheel, swinging four times every second. That’s 28,800 beats an hour, on a blue Parachrom hairspring of niobium and zirconium that shrugs off magnetism, heat and cold. And Paraflex shock absorbers guard its delicate pivots.
lines.say: And here is the heart of the watch. The balance wheel, swinging four times every second. That's twenty-eight thousand, eight hundred beats an hour, on a blue Parachrom hairspring of niobium and zirconium, that shrugs off magnetism, heat and cold. And Paraflex shock absorbers guard its delicate pivots.

lines.cap: On the dial side, the motion works turn the hour hand at one-twelfth the speed of the minute hand. And at midnight, the date doesn’t creep. It jumps, instantly.
lines.say: On the dial side, the motion works turn the hour hand at one-twelfth the speed of the minute hand. And at midnight, the date doesn't creep. It jumps! Instantly.

lines.cap: Put it all back together: the rotor winds, the spring stores, the wheels count, the escapement releases, and the balance keeps time.
lines.say: Put it all back together. The rotor winds, the spring stores, the wheels count, the escapement releases, and the balance keeps time.

lines.cap: Rolex tests every cased watch to within two seconds a day. They call it the Superlative Chronometer standard. And it does all of that without ever needing a battery.
lines.say: Rolex tests every cased watch to within two seconds a day. They call it the Superlative Chronometer standard. And it does all of that, without ever needing a battery.
